Despite your previous dislike, another reader said, "This is an action-packed story about a woman and her lover who go back in time via a time portal to 1620 AD. They save a bunch of nuns, but the clever plot twists and love of the main two characters keep the action going." What do you think?

User: No, I'm sorry, but I already have my reasons for not liking it. The review mentioned, "A trespass in Time had a decent storyline, however, it has far too many flaws to engage readers. When a lead character is a wuss, yet described as strong and independent, it doesn't gel for me. Secondary characters were bland and need development. Mostly, I did not like a town of people who would be so happy they rejoice aloud when children and others are abused in public. The attempt to translate German should have been professionally done, and if it was, fire that person. BTW, Wikipedia only has 1 K, not two as used."

Like all of Legg's books, it's very descriptive and lots of action, which makes it a good read."
